scope: Educational female lifespan mock only; no reference-range engine, no clinical inference from age. Read-only frontend review.

preferredAdultEstradiol.evidence: Supplementary Table 8, existing local full PDF/text; primary full article viewed through web PDF
preferredAdultEstradiol.method: Isotope-dilution online TurboFlow LC-MS/MS, Department of Growth and Reproduction, Rigshospitalet

recommendedIllustrativeBand.meaning: Envelope of three published calendar-phase medians; NOT full cycle amplitude, percentile interval or RI
recommendedIllustrativeBand.centerLine: No synthetic center. Optional lower line156 ONLY if explicitly identified as early follicular.

preferredAdultEstradiol.countCaution: Caption says188women but phase counts printed47+53+89=189; figure caption gives46 for early follicular. Preserve source discrepancy rather than claiming resolvedN.
preferredAdultEstradiol.postmenopause: Main article describes93 presumed postmenopausal women54.6–60.7y, mostly7–80pmol/L plus outliers; no numeric pooled median was found. Never derive median from this range.

preferredPostmenopausalEstradiol.verified: Primary PubMed/EuropePMC core abstract and publisher/PMC indexed abstract; not a full-paper extraction
preferredPostmenopausalEstradiol.population: Community-dwelling postmenopausal women, primarily European ancestry, no exogenous estrogens
preferredPostmenopausalEstradiol.method: Primarily LC-MS/MS; some extraction/chromatography RIA in one cohort; cohort results recalibrated to CDC reference measurement procedure
preferredPostmenopausalEstradiol.ageRelationship: Estradiol correlated with BMI, not chronological age in this analysis
preferredPostmenopausalEstradiol.use: A pooled postmenopausal group anchor, NOT an age-specific median or a claim of identical assay to Danish childhood/adult data.

cycleIndependentCrossCheck.citation: Anckaert et al.2021, Pract Lab Med24:e00211
cycleIndependentCrossCheck.verified: Downloaded and read full primary XML, Table1
cycleIndependentCrossCheck.method: Roche Elecsys EstradiolIII and LH, cobas e801
cycleIndependentCrossCheck.use: Source-specific cycle cross-check; do not substitute these immunoassay medians for Danish LC-MS/MS values or portray pooled phase measurements as a continuous daily median curve.

swanTransition.verified: Complete primary abstract via EuropePMC; Table1 numeric means checked in primary indexed PMC text, full HTML retrieval hit browser challenge
swanTransition.timeAxis: years relative to actual final menstrual period; cannot assign these knots to every woman at fixed chronological ages
swanTransition.use: Support timing and direction, not the amplitude of an LC-MS/MS curve. Overall meanE2 did not show a universal premenopausal rise. An E2 hump is optional individual-pattern illustration, not mandatory physiology.

alspacCrossCheck.verified: Full primary XML read, Table1 and Results/Discussion
alspacCrossCheck.use: Confirms rise around menopause and possible later fall. Premenopausal group is midlife, not general young-adult baseline; example modeled means are not observed medians.

amhInhibinTransitionCrossCheck.finding: AMH declines and low/nondetectable inhibinB already occur several years before FMP; low or undetectable inhibinB noted4–5y before FMP.
amhInhibinTransitionCrossCheck.use: Do not delay all AMH/INHB decline to the FMP or force literal0. Exact nondetection timing depends on assay sensitivity.

latePostmenopauseVariation.population: WHI OsteoPerio women not using hormone therapy
latePostmenopauseVariation.finding: Distinct FSH/LH trajectory groups include stable, declining and late-rising patterns. No universal monotonic age curve fits all postmenopausal women.
latePostmenopauseVariation.use: Broad elevated postmenopausal state is defensible; do not claim all women keep rising or all decline at one exact age.

frontendReview.reviewedOriginal: femaleDefinitions uses independently chosen infantHeight values and fixed adult tail heights; these cannot substantiate cross-age amplitudes.
recommendations: Use one display normalization per hormone after source-unit anchors are assembled; do not boost infant and adult segments independently.
ForE2 use the LC-MS/MS phase-median band156–264pmol/L with no fabricated overall mean; a pooled18pmol/L postmenopausal anchor can be separate and identified.
Inter-study connectors, ageplacement of grouped medians and transition timing remain illustrative, not an observed longitudinal trajectory.
Keep cycle bands as phase-median envelopes only if sourced; earlier arbitrary widths cannot be called real variation or RI.
Do not infer an individual menopause status, cycle phase or reproductive age from chronological age.
Do not infer pregnancy,lactation,hormone treatment or PCOS trajectories from this baseline female overview.
